data_selectors.note: bank-picker's institution row (found on device): RN merges the row's name and subtitle Text siblings into one accessibility label, so the selector must be the whole merged string, not just the institution name.
settings-banks' connected-bank row (found on device): ConnectedBankRow merges the bank name and the 'Al día' status badge (home.banks_badge_ok) into one accessibility label.
Merchant name from stage-queue-v1.sql's stage-tx-income row — tapped to open merchant-edit.

notifications-schedule's time-step heading (found on device): the screen composes a decorative glyph (a JS constant, not an i18n key — see notifications-schedule.tsx's own CLOCK_GLYPH comment) and notifications_schedule.time_title in one Text, merging them into one accessibility label.
notifications-schedule's days-step heading (found on device): same composition as the time-step heading, with CALENDAR_GLYPH and notifications_schedule.days_title.

The settings hub's 'Acerca de' row (re-confirmed on device during the #22 closing task's round-2 run): SETTINGS_HUB_ROWS composes a ListRow whose title and subtitle merge into one accessibility label ('Acerca de, Versión 0.0.0' — the subtitle is no longer empty on this build, unlike this entry's original note). Maestro's `tapOn`/`assertVisible` text selector is a full-string (anchored) regex match, not a substring search, so the trailing `.*` is required to match the subtitle remainder regardless of its exact value.

The settings hub's 'Perfil local' row (re-confirmed on device during the #22 closing task's round-2 run) — same ListRow merging as 'Acerca de, .*' ('Perfil local, Sin bancos conectados'), with the same full-match rationale for the trailing `.*`.
The 'freelance' category's Spanish display name (design/tokens.json categoryLabels.income), suggested for stage-tx-income by its merchant's default category.

The Expo dev-client's own native launcher chrome (English regardless of app locale, not app copy) — shared/fixture.yaml taps this row to reconnect to Metro after a launchApp(clearState) cold-starts the launcher instead of the JS app (confirmed on device).
